info.title: JSON-Pure WebAPI for MT4/MT5
info.description:
Works with MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 trade servers and keeps a live connection to each of them, so the `…Get` calls answer from it much faster than the `…Request` calls, which ask the trade server every time.

Partly follows the JSON-Pure API idea: a successful call answers HTTP 200; any other code reports an error, such as wrong parameters or an unavailable trade platform.

servers.description: Sandbox — free, no SLA, may be reset

get.description:
Server time of the connected MT4 trade server.
            
Smoke-test endpoint exercising the v2 envelope. Returns current MT4
server time wrapped in ApiResponse<DateTime>.

**Timeout:** 10 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

The complete server record: identity, protocol version, socket and
feed timeouts, bind and web address lists, storage paths, runtime
counters, and the operational subsystems (demo accounts, rollover,
statements, live update).
            
Requires the sensitive-settings permission: the record describes the
server's infrastructure, not only its public identity.

get.description:
The common server record as the configuration system returns it, read live from
the trade server on every call.
            
Same fields as `ManagerCommonEx`; the difference is the source: this call
goes through the configuration interface rather than the manager connection, and
is the read that `CfgUpdateCommon` writes back.
            
Requires the settings permission, not the sensitive one — a client that may
change common settings but not read the server's infrastructure can still use it.

**Timeout:** 10 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

post.description:
Change server-wide common settings. Only the fields present in the body are written: the
current record is read from the trade server, the body is applied over it, and the merged
record is written back. A field that is left out keeps its server value; for the string
fields, omitting the key keeps the value while sending `""` clears it. A body without
any field is rejected.
            
Preserved fields the DTO does not touch:
<list type="bullet"><item>Runtime counters (LastOrder, LastLogin, LostLogin,
        optimization timestamps, overnight rollover state).</item><item>Protocol identity (ServerVersion, ServerBuild).</item><item>Bind / web address arrays (variable-length nested
        collections — own endpoints planned).</item><item>Demo-account subsystem, paths, rollover/statement modes
        (sensitive admin areas with separate endpoints).</item></list>
            
Idempotency-Key strongly recommended — overwriting common settings
affects every connected client.

**Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

get.description:
All holiday-calendar entries configured on the MT4 server, paginated.
            
Manager-live read (round-trip). Holidays describe trading-suspension
dates per symbol or symbol-group. Each entry carries date components
(Year/Month/Day), a work-time window (From/To, minutes from midnight,
both 0 for full closure), the affected Symbol (or "All"), a free-form
Description, and an Enable flag. Ordering: by (Year, Month, Day, From,
Symbol) ascending so cursors are stable and unique. The cursor is an
opaque base64 string produced by CursorCodec from the composite
"{YYYYMMDD * 10000 + From:D14}|{Symbol}" key — the Symbol tiebreaker
covers the case where multiple holidays share date and From minute
(per-symbol partial-day closures), guaranteeing pagination never drops
rows even inside same-(date,From) clusters.

**Timeout:** 10 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

get.description:
Server access-hour matrix (per-hour 7×24 allow/deny grid) from the MT4 server's `ConTime` configuration.
            
Manager-live read (round-trip). Returns `MT4ServerTime` with
a flat 168-element `AccessHours` array; each element is 0
(denied) or 1 (allowed) for one hour of the week. Layout:
`index = day*24 + hour`, day 0 = Sunday (MT4 convention).
Internal `DaysControl` and `Reserved` platform fields
are not surfaced.

**Timeout:** 10 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

post.description:
Update the 7×24 access-hour matrix — Type 1 mutator.
            
Manager (live) call. Reads the current `ConTime`, replaces the
168-hour access matrix with the supplied `AccessHours`, and
writes back. The platform's internal `DaysControl` (server
housekeeping) and `Reserved` (forward-compat padding) fields
are preserved across the round-trip.
            
`AccessHours` must be exactly 168 entries long; index =
`day * 24 + hour` with day 0 = Sunday. Each value is
`0` (denied) or `1` (allowed) — any other value is
passed through verbatim (the platform does not validate, and
MT4 may treat anything non-zero as allowed depending on build).
            
Echoes the merged `MT4ServerTime` in the response.

**Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

requestBody.description: Replacement access matrix. `AccessHours.Length` must be 168.

schema.description:
v2 DTO for the MT4 server's per-hour access matrix (the platform's `ConTime.Days` field). 168-element flat array; each element is `0` (denied) or `1` (allowed) for one hour of the week. Layout: `index = day * 24 + hour`, day-of-week 0..6 matches MT4's native convention where day 0 = Sunday.
Example: `AccessHours[24..47]` covers Monday's 24 hours. Internal `DaysControl` and `Reserved` platform fields are not part of the v2 contract.

get.description:
All firewall (IP access) rules configured on the MT4 server, paginated.
            
Manager-live read (round-trip). Each entry describes an IP range
(IpFrom..IpTo, widened uint→long for JSON safety) with an Action
flag and a free-form Comment. Ordering: by (IpFrom, IpTo) ascending.
Cursor is an opaque base64 string holding the composite key
"{IpFrom:D10}|{IpTo:D10}" — D10 width matches uint range (max
4_294_967_295 = 10 digits) so lexicographic compare matches
numeric compare, and the '|' delimiter cannot appear in IP values.

**Timeout:** 10 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

MT4 server backup configuration (full + archive + export schedules, watchdog HA pair settings).
            
Manager-live read (round-trip). Returns the platform's ConBackup as
MT4Backup DTO — full/archive/export schedule enums and paths, last
completion timestamps, and HA-watchdog fields. The platform's
`WatchPassword` (slave-server credential) is intentionally
dropped from the v2 contract for security and is NOT present in
the response payload.

**Timeout:** 10 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

post.description: Update server backup configuration — Type 1 mutator. Manager (live) call. Reads the current `ConBackup`, overlays the fields in `MT4Backup` onto it, and writes back via `CfgUpdateBackup`. Two classes of preserved fields: Slave-server credential — `WatchPassword` stays whatever the platform read live. It is unreachable from the v2 request body (DTO does not expose it).Last-completion timestamps — `FullBackupLastTime`, `ArchiveLastTime`, `ExportLastTime`, `WatchTimestamp`. Server-derived runtime state that clients must not overwrite. Echoes the merged `MT4Backup` in the response. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Update a chart-history synchronization rule — Type 1 mutator.
            
Manager (live) call. Sync configurations are paged on the read
side (see `CfgRequestSync`); the v2 contract identifies a
rule by the composite key `(Server, Login)`. Flow:
<list type="number"><item>Read the current list via `CfgRequestSync`.</item><item>Find the entry whose `(Server, Login)` matches the
        body. Missing entry → NotFound envelope.</item><item>Apply DTO overlay onto the matched entry — the
        replication credential (`Password`) carried by the
        live struct is preserved.</item><item>Write the merged struct back.</item></list>
Echoes the merged `MT4Sync` in the response.

**Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

Update a LiveUpdate service configuration — Type 1 mutator.
            
Manager (live) call. LiveUpdate entries are paged on the read side
(see `CfgRequestLiveUpdate`); the v2 contract identifies an
entry by its `Company` field (same cursor key the read
endpoint uses). Flow: read live list → match by `Company` →
overlay → write back. The 128-element `Files` descriptor

post.description:
Update an IP firewall rule at a given list position — Type 1 mutator.
            
Manager (live) call. The platform's `CfgUpdateAccess(cfg, pos)`
signature requires a position rather than a unique-key lookup (the
rule table has no stable identifiers — multiple rules can carry the
same range/action/comment). The v2 endpoint exposes the position as
a route parameter; callers must read the current list via
`CfgRequestAccess` first and pass the index of the row to
update. Flow:
<list type="number"><item>Read the live list via `CfgRequestAccess`.</item><item>Bounds-check `pos` against the list length — out of
        range yields a NotFound envelope.</item><item>Apply DTO overlay onto `list[pos]`.</item><item>Write back with `CfgUpdateAccess(merged, pos)`.</item></list>`IpFrom`/`IpTo` in the body must fit in `[0, uint.MaxValue]`
— out-of-range values are rejected with `errorCode=Validation`
before anything is written.

**Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

get.description:
Time series of MT4 server resource snapshots — CPU, memory, network, sockets, connected-users — captured at server-defined cadence.
            
Manager-live read (round-trip to MT4 server). The MT4 server records
these snapshots periodically (typically every five minutes, broker-
configurable). Pass from as the earliest timestamp
to include; the server returns every snapshot at or after that point
up to the present, in ascending `Ctm` order. Useful for capacity
dashboards, oncall incident timelines, and load investigations. Pump
cache is NOT consulted — data reflects the authoritative server log.
Returns an empty list (Ok envelope, not an error) when the window
contains no snapshots.

**Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

parameters.name: tradePlatform
parameters.description: Trade platform id (GUID)

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Window start timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601). Snapshots with
             `Ctm >= from` are returned. Marshalled to the platform as
             `__time32_t` — values before 1970 or after 2038 are out of range.

parameters.name: X-Request-Timeout
parameters.description: How long to wait for the trade server, in seconds (1–300). Default for this operation: 30 s (history or report). The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.

get.description:
Closed-trade reports for a batch of account logins within a time window — the data set that drives broker financial reporting (PnL, commissions, taxes) and customer trade-history exports.
            
Manager-live read (round-trip to MT4 server). Pass logins as repeated
query parameters: `?logins=1001&logins=1002&logins=1003`.
Server-side billing counts this as one Manager request regardless of
batch size — prefer one batched call over a per-login loop.
            
The platform returns a dictionary keyed by order ticket; the v2 envelope
flattens it to a list. Missing logins are silently omitted (no error
envelope). The optional name parameter selects a
server-defined report template — leave it null/empty to use the
default `"RTL_report"` template (closed trades within the window).
            
Pump cache is NOT consulted — data reflects authoritative server
history. Note: the platform comment warns that asking for a window
where the manager account lacks the `Reports` permission may
cause MT4 to drop the manager connection; this endpoint guards that
indirectly via the API-side `ResourceAccess` check, but a broker
that mis-configured the underlying manager rights can still observe
transient connection bounces.

**Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

parameters.description: Window start (UTC, ISO 8601 — required)

parameters.description: Window end (UTC, ISO 8601 — required)

parameters.name: logins
parameters.description:
Account logins to include (repeat the query
             parameter for batch — must be non-empty)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Report template name (max 32 chars). Defaults to
             `"RTL_report"` when null or empty.

The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.

get.description:
End-of-day balance/equity/PnL snapshots for a batch of account logins within a date window — the broker daily-report data set, flat shape (one row per (login, day) pair).
            
Manager-live read (round-trip to MT4 server). Pass logins as repeated
query parameters: `?logins=1001&logins=1002&logins=1003`.
Server-side billing counts this as one Manager request regardless of
batch size — prefer one batched call over a per-login loop.
            
Each row carries its own `Login` field, so the flat shape is
joinable on the client side. The MT4 server returns dates in its
local time zone, **not** UTC — clients should treat `Ctm` as
"broker day boundary" and convert as appropriate.
            
Note: the platform warns that asking for a window where the manager
account lacks the `Automatic server reports` permission may
cause MT4 to drop the manager connection. The API-side
`ResourceAccess` check is an indirect guard; a broker that
mis-configured the underlying manager rights can still observe
transient connection bounces.

**Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

Same data set as `DailyReportsRequest`, but server-side grouped by login. Convenience shape for clients that pivot the data per-account (per-day rollups, account dashboards).
            
Manager-live read — single round-trip to MT4 server, identical billing
cost to `DailyReportsRequest`. The platform returns a sorted-list
of sorted-lists (by login, then by date); the v2 envelope flattens
the inner list to a chronologically-ordered `MT4DailyReport`
array, leaving the outer keying by login.
            
JSON shape: `{ "817542": [ ... ], "1001": [ ... ] }` — JSON
object keys are strings, so int logins are stringified. Clients
should parse keys back to int if needed.

post.description:
Opens a server-side incremental sync session for daily reports modified at or after timestamp. Follow up with `DailySyncRead` to retrieve the snapshot.
            
Manager-live POST (modifies server-side session state). The two-call
cycle `DailySyncStart → DailySyncRead` is the broker pattern for
pulling only-changed-since-last-poll daily reports; pass
`timestamp=0` to request all records.
            
`timestamp` is a Unix epoch second (int32) in MT4 server-local
time, not UTC. Platform marshals it directly to `__time32_t` —
pre-1970 / post-2038 values are out of range.
            
Returns a bare success envelope (no payload); the actual data comes
from a subsequent `DailySyncRead` call.

**Timeout:** 60 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Drains the daily-report snapshot opened by the most recent `DailySyncStart` call. Returns every record reserved by the server in that sync session.

valid response when the snapshot held no records; this is NOT an
error.
            
Call `DailySyncStart` first; calling `DailySyncRead` without
a prior `DailySyncStart` may return an empty list or a non-Ok
`managerAPICode` depending on server build.

fields (operation type, command, symbol, volume, price), submits via POST,

back. Each field lists its valid names.

Pump-cached call. Cancels a pending trade transaction that the
MT4 server is still holding in the rollback buffer (e.g. an
instant-execution requote that has not yet been confirmed). Has
no effect once the transaction has been committed; returns the
the platform's `ResultCode` as part of the envelope on failure.
            
Idempotent on already-committed/already-rolled-back tickets.

post.description:
Submit a trade transaction — open / modify / close / balance op.
POST mutator covering every platform trade operation through the single `TradeTransaction` entry point. The request body's `tradeTransactionType` + `tradeCommand` combination selects the actual operation — `OpenMarket`+`Buy`, `PendingOpen`+`BuyLimit`, `CloseMarket`+`Sell`, and the manager-side `Br*` types: `BrModify` (open price, SL, TP of an order), `BrDelete`, `BrBalance`+`Balance` or `Credit` (balance/credit operation on `orderBy`). The schema of the request body lists every accepted value.
An unknown `tradeTransactionType`, `tradeCommand` or `tradeRequestFlags` value is refused with error code `Validation` and the list of valid values; nothing is sent to the trading platform. Names are case-insensitive; the numeric value of a member is accepted too.
On success the response echoes the platform's mutated structure — most importantly the `Order` field, which the server assigns on Open operations and clients use to track the ticket afterwards.
Idempotency-Key is essentially mandatory. A retried trade transaction without the header can open a second position, double- close, or apply a balance op twice. With the header the second call returns the cached envelope from the first. **Timeout:** 5 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Set the account password — Type 1 mutator (direct overwrite). POST body: the new password as a JSON string. Optional query params: `changeInvestor=true` sets the read-only investor password instead of the primary one; `cleanPubkey=true` resets the public key alongside the password (caller's RSA-protected secondary auth).
This is a Type 1 mutator — full-replace semantics. The platform accepts the new password directly without a read-modify-write loop. There is no Type 2 ("set only this field, leave the rest alone") variant of password change because the password is itself a single field — the read step would be tautological.
Idempotency-Key is strongly recommended. A retried password change without the header risks setting it twice (the second call returns success even though the password is the same), which is harmless but generates audit noise. With the header, the second call short-circuits to the cached response. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Change an account. The `login` field of the body identifies the account and is never
changed; the response is a boolean.
            
Only the fields present in the body are written: the record is read live from the trade
server, the body is applied over it, and the merged record is written back. A field that
is left out keeps its server value; for the string fields, omitting the key keeps the
value while sending `""` clears it. Server-assigned and secret values (passwords, OTP
secret, registration date, last login, previous-period balances) always keep their server
values. A body with the login but no field to change is rejected.
            
Idempotency-Key strongly recommended: a change to the account affects
trading immediately, and a blind retry can overwrite concurrent edits.

**Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

Manager (live) call. The MT4 server walks the symbol's full bar
history for every period and fixes inconsistencies (gaps, broken

kick off a second full sweep.

post.description:
Plugin custom-command channel with JSON payload in both directions.
            
Manager (live) call wrapping `ExternalCommandJSON`. The MT4
server forwards the body to whichever installed plugin claims the
command first; the first plugin returning `RET_OK` wins and its
response becomes the v2 payload. The request body is sent verbatim
(no field renaming, no schema enforcement) so the plugin author
owns the over-the-wire contract on both ends.
            
The platform trio (`ExternalCommand<TIn,TOut>` for binary
marshal, `ExternalCommandCustom<T>` for caller-supplied
serializer) is intentionally not exposed in v2 — those variants
require compile-time struct layouts shared between client and
plugin, which a REST surface cannot guarantee. Plugin developers
who need binary transport should keep using the platform directly
from the WebAPI process or build a dedicated binary endpoint.
            
Idempotency-Key is strongly recommended — plugins may have side
effects, and the channel itself gives no read-modify-write
semantics.

**Timeout:** 60 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Bulk-deletes a list of trade tickets (administrative scope). Used for cleanup after reconciliation mistakes, simulator state reset, or compliance-mandated removal.

tickets and a count; we mirror the existing batched-int pattern
(repeat `?orders=` per ticket — same convention as
`UserRecordsRequest`'s `?logins=`). Empty arrays are
rejected with Validation.

server's trade table; this is not reversible from the API side.
Pair with `Idempotency-Key` so retries don't re-process partial
failures.

is internal/private, so this v2 endpoint re-implements the check
directly: enumerate the full group catalog via

names are case-sensitive in the underlying API).

get.description:
OHLC bars of a symbol for a time window, ordered by time ascending. The trade server keeps history as minutes; bars of a coarser `period` are aggregated from those minutes on the boundaries of the server's trading time, so a day starts at 00:00 of the server clock. A bar opens with the first minute of the bucket and closes with the last one, its high and low are the extremes of the bucket, tick volume and real volume are summed, and spread is the lowest of the bucket. Buckets without minutes are not produced.
Times are the trading times of the trade server, not UTC: `time` repeats the seconds-from-1970 value the platform uses, `dateTime` is the same moment without an offset. Prices are returned as the platform holds them, without rescaling.
`from` and `to` are optional: without `from` the window starts at the beginning of the history, without `to` it ends at the current server time. `limit` is 0 by default and returns the whole window; a positive value caps the returned bars and sets `truncated`. There is no pagination: to read further, repeat the request with `from` moved past the last returned bar.
The call only reads and changes nothing. When the platform has not received the requested history yet, the call fails with the platform code `MT_RET_OK_NONE` and a message saying the history is not synchronized — such a request may be repeated later. `W1` and `MN1` are rejected: such bars are not built. **Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

The call blocks while the dealer answer is awaited. When the answer does not arrive before the server timeout, the platform error `MT_RET_ERR_TIMEOUT` is returned. post.description:

post.summary: Rescan the access points of the trade server
post.description:
Forces a scan of the access points of the trade server — the network map with the load of
each access server and the ping to it — and reports whether a better access point than the
current one was found. The scan is rate-limited by the platform to one request per half an
hour; a call inside that window is answered with the platform error that says so.
            
The answer says what was found, not what was done: the connection is not switched. Moving
the connection to the found access point is a separate step of the connection management.
A zero `timeout` checks for a better point without waiting for the scan to finish.

**Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.summary: Write a settings file of the manager account
post.description:
Stores the file in the directory of the manager account on the trade server, replacing a
file of the same name wholly. The server does not track changes made by other applications:
only the last submitted version is kept, so the whole file is sent, not just the changed
values.
            
One level of nesting and at most 128 folders are available inside the manager directory, at
most 1024 files are kept, and each file is limited to 16 MB — a larger payload is refused as
invalid. Only the file name extensions the platform accepts may be used; it answers an
unknown one with the error that explains it. Send updates sparingly: the platform advises
no more than one update per five minutes.

**Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

description of the address range it belongs to: geography, network owner and the additional
characteristics of the address.

Writes the fields present in the body to the group with the given name. Only the fields the trading platform lets a manager change are accepted: the margin call level, the stop out level, the mode used to check them and the group trade options. A field left out of the body keeps its current value, and a body without any field is rejected.
The configuration is read from the trade server first, the body is applied over it and the result is written back, so a request never overwrites values it does not mention. The answer carries the configuration stored by the server after the write. Commission settings and per-symbol overrides are not part of this body.
The change is accepted only from the main trade server and only for a manager holding the rights to group margin and commission settings; any other case is answered with the platform error code. Repeat the request to retry after a failure that reported no result. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. get.summary: Get the raw tick stream of a symbol
get.description:
Returns the stored quotes of the symbol for a time window, both the raw ones and the processed ones the symbol configuration produces, ordered by time ascending. When the symbol stores raw quotes, the stream is denser than the one `TicksHistory` returns.
Times are the trading times of the trade server, not UTC. `from` is required — a window without a start would scan the whole stored history. `to` is optional and defaults to the current server time. `limit` is 0 by default and returns the whole window; a positive value caps the returned ticks and sets `truncated`. There is no pagination: to read further, repeat the request with `from` moved past the last returned tick.
The call only reads and changes nothing. When the platform has not received the requested history yet, the call fails with the platform code `MT_RET_OK_NONE` and a message saying the history is not synchronized — such a request may be repeated later.
The window is limited to one day and the answer to one million ticks, because the whole history of that window is materialised by the trade server interface before the `limit` is applied. Ask for a day at a time and continue from the last tick returned; a longer window is refused rather than served at the risk of the service's memory. **Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

post.description:
Drops every open session of the given login. The terminals of the account reconnect on their own afterwards, so the account appears in the connection list again within a short time unless its access is closed.
Forced disconnection is the way to make new account settings take effect at once — a terminal keeps the settings it loaded at login. The call answers `true` when every session of the login was dropped; a login without open sessions answers the platform "not found" error. Repeating the call is harmless. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. post.summary: Disconnect several clients from the trade server
post.description:
Drops every open session of every login in the body. Each login is processed on its own: the answer carries its outcome, so one login that could not be dropped does not hide the result of the others. Duplicates in the body are collapsed, and logins without open sessions are reported as "not found".
The answer is a list with one entry per requested login, in request order. The call is safe to repeat: a login that was already dropped answers "not found" and changes nothing. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:

A refused subscription — disabled configuration, account not allowed, no money — is returned as the platform error that explains it.

post.summary: Open the queue of trade requests for dealing
post.description:
Subscribes the connection to the queue of trade requests of the trade server and loads the requests already waiting in it. From that moment the queue can be read and the requests can be taken for processing — by this connection only, and the subscription lives until the queue is closed or the connection is lost.
The call does not take a request and does not answer one: it only enables the queue. Repeating it on a connection whose queue is already open is harmless. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.summary: Close the queue of trade requests
post.description:
Stops dealing on the connection: the queue is no longer read or taken from, and the requests waiting in it stay in the queue for other dealers. Requests already taken for processing are not returned to the queue — they must still be answered.
The queue applies to the whole connection to the trade platform, so closing it affects every call that reads or takes requests from it. Repeating the call is harmless. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.summary: Take the first request of the queue for processing
post.description:
Takes the request at the head of the queue and reserves it for this connection: the trade server will not hand it to another dealer and waits for the answer. The request must be answered with `DealerAnswer`; an unanswered request is not returned to the queue and is lost.
The call is a write, not a read for all practical purposes: it changes the state of the queue and cannot be safely repeated — a repeated call takes the next request. When the queue is empty the platform answers `MT_RET_OK_NONE`. The queue must be opened with `DealerStart` first. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

`MT_RET_OK_NONE` means that the request is no longer available: it has already been taken by another dealer or has been processed. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.summary: Bring orders, positions and balance of an account in line with an external system
post.description:
Makes the orders, positions and balance of the account match the passed state. The trade server compares the lists with its own data and performs the difference as deals with the `sync` reason: positions missing on one side are opened or closed, positions whose direction, price or contract size changed are reopened, a volume change is corrected, and a balance difference becomes a balance or correction deal. All of it stays in the trading history of the client.
The operation is heavy and changes money and positions: it must be used by the system that owns the account, not as a general-purpose edit. An omitted order or position list leaves that part untouched; an empty list states that the account has none and closes the existing ones. The call answers as soon as the trade server has accepted it, and the resulting state of the account is reported to the platform journal. **Timeout:** 5 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

Stores a deal in the trade database of the connected server without trading it: the
balance of the account is not changed by the call itself, the record is simply written.
The ticket, when given, must fall inside the deal ticket range of the server and be above

post.description:
Creates a trading account on the trade server. Every field of the record is optional: a field left out is not written to the new account, so it keeps the value the platform starts it with — and that value is `None` for rights, so an account created without `rights` cannot log in until the flag is granted. Send `rights` (at least `Enabled`) to make the account usable. A real trade server also refuses creation without a leverage (`MT_RET_ERR_PARAMS`): send `leverage` together with the group.
When the login field is absent or zero the server allocates one from the available range; when no logins are left the call fails with the platform error `MT_RET_USR_LOGIN_EXHAUSTED`. The group must be set, as well as the first or the last name of the account holder; otherwise the call fails with `MT_RET_ERR_PARAMS`. Adding an account whose login already exists fails with `MT_RET_USR_LOGIN_EXIST`.
Passwords are checked against the group policy. When either the master or the investor password is absent, both are regenerated to the group minimum length; a password the policy refuses is replaced with a fresh pair and the creation is repeated up to ten times. A failure of any other kind ends the call at once — a retry after a timeout could create a second account, since the first attempt may have succeeded unseen. The response carries the record as stored by the server, including the allocated login. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Pass arbitrary binary payload to the MT4 server's plugin pipeline.
Manager (live) call via the platform's `ExternalCommandCustom` overload with a pass-through byte-array marshaller. The first installed plugin that returns `RET_OK` wins; its response bytes become the payload's `Data` field.
Wire format: `byte[]` serializes as base64 in JSON. Clients agree with the plugin author on the binary layout.
Why sidecar-only: the platform's binary variants rely on `Marshal.SizeOf` + native `ExternalCommand` dispatch. On `mtmanapi64.dll` the signed/unsigned marshalling diverges from `mtmanapi.dll` — same payload byte-for-byte can decode differently on x64. The x86 sidecar process loads the 32-bit DLL where the marshalling is the original one.
The platform's third `ExternalCommandCustom` overload that takes an `ICustomSerializer` interface is genuinely not REST-translatable — it requires the caller to provide C# serialization logic in-process. Not exposed. **Timeout:** 60 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

Must be preceded by `POST UsersSyncStart` on the main x64
API to seed the server-side snapshot. Same UnpackObject hazard
as `UsersSnapshot` — sidecar-only.

MT4Group.description:
v2 DTO describing a trading group configuration. Curated subset of the
the platform's `ConGroup` — exposes the configuration fields that callers
need to inspect margin/leverage/rights settings.
            
Deliberately omitted from v2 (vs v1's full ConGroup shape):
  * `SmtpServer`, `SmtpLogin`, `SmtpPassword` — SMTP
    credentials must never cross the v2 boundary regardless of access
    level. `SmtpServer` alone is dropped too because a server name
    is rarely useful without its credentials and exposes infra topology.
  * `Templates` — server-side filesystem path, irrelevant to API
    consumers and a minor information-disclosure risk.
  * `SecuritiesHash` — opaque byte[], platform bookkeeping.
  * `Reserved`, `UnusedRights`, `SecGroups[32]`,
    `SecMargins[128]` — reserved/internal arrays. The two nested
    arrays (SecGroups, SecMargins) deserve their own dedicated v2
    endpoints (`GroupSecGroupsGet/{group}`, `GroupSecMarginsGet/{group}`)
    planned for Wave 3 — including them here would balloon the DTO.
  * `NewsLanguages` (uint[]) and `NewsLanguagesTotal` —
    rarely consumed; can be added later once the use case is clear.
            
Enums (`OTPMode`, `MarginMode`, `NewsMode`,
`MarginControllingType`) are returned as their names;
`GroupRights` is a flags string, the names of the set bits.

MT4SymbolConfigUpdate.description:
Type 1 mutator input for `CfgUpdateSymbol`. Same field set as the read
DTO MT4SymbolConfig minus:
  * `Symbol` (path parameter, immutable identity);
  * `Count`, `CountOriginal`, `FilterCounter` — server-side
    counters, derived;
  * Enum fields are submitted as their names.
            
Fields preserved by the server-side read step (NOT on this DTO):
  * `Symbol` identity.
  * `Sessions` nested array (own endpoint planned).

    `FilterReserved` reserved arrays.
  * `Count`, `CountOriginal`, `FilterCounter`,
    `BidTickValue`, `AskTickValue`, `Point`, `Multiply`
    — server-derived from other fields, writing them is a no-op or
    overwrite-with-stale.

MT4TradeTransaction.description:
v2 DTO for a trade transaction — input AND output of `TradeTransaction`.
The platform's `TradeTransInfo` is in/out: the caller fills the request
fields (operation type, command, symbol, volume, price), submits via POST,
and the server populates the resulting `Order` id (for Open) or
echoes the modified record (for Modify/Close).
            
Enum fields (`TradeTransactionType`, `TradeCommand`,
`TradeRequestFlags`) are plain strings. Clients submit the name
(e.g. `"Buy"`, `"PendingOpen"`); the response echoes the names
back. Each field lists its valid names.

Type 1 mutator input for the admin direct-edit endpoint `AdmTradeRecordModify`. Only the fields a back-office tool would legitimately need to adjust are exposed; everything else (order id, login, symbol, volume, open/close times, gateway internals, conversion rates, API data blobs) is preserved from the server-side read.

MT4User.description:
v2 DTO describing a trading account. Curated subset of the platform's
`UserRecord` — exposes identity, contact, financial and flag fields
that callers actually need.
            
Deliberately omitted from v2 (vs v1's full UserRecord shape):
  * Password / PasswordInvestor / PasswordPhone / OtpSecret / ApiData /
    SecureReserved — credentials and secrets must never cross the v2
    boundary regardless of access level.
  * Unused / Reserved2 / EnableReserved / TimeStamp — platform bookkeeping
    with no caller-visible semantics.
            
Account flags are exposed as a single MT4User.EnableFlags bitfield
(the platform's native representation). Bit semantics are documented under
that property — splitting it into separate booleans would hide the fact
that MetaQuotes occasionally reuses bit positions across builds.

MT4UserCreate.description:
Type 1 mutator input — full create shape for `UserRecordNew`.
Same writable fields as MT4UserUpdate minus the explicit
`Balance`/`Credit` (those should come through dedicated balance
operations after the account exists). The platform allocates the next free
login id when `Login = 0`; clients may also request a specific id by
setting `Login > 0` (the server rejects collisions).
            
Password / OTP / API-data fields are NOT on this DTO. After successful
creation, set the initial password via a separate
`POST UserPasswordSet/{login}` call. The platform accepts the new
account with empty password bytes; the password endpoint lifts it to
usable credentials.

priceCost.description: Real cost of the subscription, the amount the client is actually charged.

countries.description: Countries the subscription is available in.

groups.description: Account groups the subscription is available in.

MT5ConSubscriptionFlags.description:
Additional properties of a subscription configuration.
Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Enable, AutoProlong"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit" (bit number). Bits: Enable = 0x1, AutoProlong = 0x2. Accepted on input, never written: All = Enable, AutoProlong.

level.description:

tickHistory.description:
Depth of the tick history available by the subscription.
One of: None, LastDay, LastWeek, LastMonth, Last3Months, Last6Months, LastYear, Last2Years, Last3Years, Last5Years, All. Case-insensitive; the numeric value is accepted too. Any other value is refused with error code Validation.

credit.description: Amount of credit funds of the account at the report time.

dailyCredit.description: Credit given to the account during the reported day.

orders.description: Pending orders of the account; `null` in a lightweight report.

tiers.description: Tiers of the rule, ordered by range start.

rangeTo.description: End of the range; zero means the range is open-ended.

marginRateInitial.description: Initial margin rate charged inside the range.

marginRateMaintenance.description: Maintenance margin rate charged inside the range.

MT5LeverageTier.description: Tier of a floating margin rule: one range and the margin rates inside it.

Bits: Close = 0x1, Market = 0x2, ChangedPrice = 0x4, ChangedTrigger = 0x8, ChangedSL = 0x10, ChangedTP = 0x20, ChangedExpType = 0x40, ChangedExpTime = 0x80, Expert = 0x100, Signal = 0x200, SkipMarginCheck = 0x400. Accepted on input, never written: All = Close, Market, ChangedPrice, ChangedTrigger, ChangedSL, ChangedTP, ChangedExpType, ChangedExpTime, Expert, Signal, SkipMarginCheck.

TradeActivationFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("NoLimit, NoStop"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: NoLimit = 0x1, NoStop = 0x2, NoSLimit = 0x4, NoSL = 0x8, NoTP = 0x10, NoSO = 0x20, NoExpiration = 0x40. Accepted on input, never written: All = NoLimit, NoStop, NoSLimit, NoSL, NoTP, NoSO, NoExpiration.

TradeModifyFlags.description:
also used for Deal,Order,Position
Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Admin, Manager"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit" (bit number). tags.name: MT4ControllerV
tags.description:
MT4 v2 — clean envelope, structured errors, Idempotency-Key
header support, cache-hit billing exemption, path-based versioning.
See https://cloud.mywebapi.com/history for the customer-facing migration guide.

tags.name: MT4DealerControllerV
tags.description:
MT4 v2 — dealing-office reports: symbol summaries, currency exposure,
profit calculation and the Manager API log.

tags.name: MT5AdminControllerV
tags.description: MT5 v2 — dealer operations and bulk configuration reads.

tags.name: MT5ClientsControllerV
tags.description:
MT5 v2 — client records of the trade server as kept for a CRM: the clients themselves, the
accounts bound to them, their documents, the comments on both and the files attached to them.

tags.name: MT5CommsControllerV
tags.description:
MT5 v2 — communications and service operations of the trade server: internal mail, news,
application license checks, journal, network state, settings files, custom commands,
IP address resolution and the proxy of the manager connection.

tags.name: MT5ConfigControllerV
tags.description: MT5 v2 — configuration changes of groups, symbols and server time.

tags.name: MT5ConfigTradeControllerV
tags.description: MT5 v2 — trading configuration: floating margin and plugin settings.

tags.name: MT5ControllerV
tags.description:
MT5 v2 — clean envelope, structured errors, Idempotency-Key
header support, cache-hit billing exemption, path-based versioning.
See https://cloud.mywebapi.com/history for the customer-facing migration guide.

tags.name: MT5DealsControllerV
tags.description: MT5 v2 deals, positions and their bulk maintenance operations.

tags.name: MT5MarketDataControllerV
tags.description:
MT5 v2 — quotes and price history of the trade server: reads of the current quote and of
the stored history, and writes that change the stored history.

tags.name: MT5MarketInsightControllerV
tags.description: MT5 v2 — live connections, the selected-symbol list and the Depth of Market.

tags.name: MT5OrdersControllerV
tags.description:
MT5 v2 — orders of the trade database (active, pending and historical),
with the clean v2 response envelope and structured errors.
See https://cloud.mywebapi.com/history for the customer-facing migration guide.

tags.name: MT5ReportsControllerV
tags.description:
MT5 v2 — daily reports of client accounts, the summary of client and hedging positions
and the exposure of the company.

tags.name: MT5SubscriptionsControllerV
tags.description: MT5 v2 — subscriptions of trading accounts and subscription configurations.

tags.name: MT5TradeOpsControllerV
tags.description: MT5 v2 — dealing with the queue of trade requests and the auxiliary trading calculations.

tags.name: MT5TradingControllerV
tags.description:
MT5 v2 — writes to the trading database (orders, positions and deals) and the reads that
ask the trade server for a fresh record instead of answering from the pump cache.

tags.name: MT5UsersControllerV
tags.description: MT5 v2 — user and client records.

tags.name: MT5UsersExtrasControllerV

MT5 v2 — account certificates, external accounts, balance reconciliation, bulk account
operations and outgoing messages.
